review.algorithm_assessment: For a nonnegative order statistic, expectation equals the integral of its survival probability. Between consecutive interval endpoints each variable is certainly above, certainly below, or has a linear probability of exceeding x. A polynomial Bernoulli-count DP computes the probability that at least K variables exceed x. Integrate every coefficient exactly in the prime field over that interval, including the initial interval from0. No floating-point approximation or Monte Carlo is used.

 sure=sum(l>=right for l,r in ranges);active=[(r-left,inv) for (l,r),inv in zip(ranges,denominators) if l<=left<r];need=k-sure;width=right-left

 if need>len(active):continue
 dp=[[1]]
 for numerator,inv in active:
  q=numerator*inv%MOD;b=(-inv)%MOD;new=[[0]*(len(dp[0])+1) for _ in range(len(dp)+1)]
  for count,poly in enumerate(dp):
   for degree,value in enumerate(poly):

print(answer%MOD)
